label: Chill
example: The turkey walks across the yard and stops in front of the barn.

label: Slang
example: Bro, this turkey ain't got no chill - he's straight up strutting to the barn.
register_note: Brief 11, Task 4: two markers from ONE group suffice — "ain't gonna" is two reduced forms and reads perfectly as slang.

label: Ironic
forbidden: irony in the correct answer or distractors of a sentence exercise
naming an object that competes with the correct answer
on ironic_keyword_types: quotation marks on the correct option only
example: A very humble entrance, obviously. The whole yard is honoured.

label: Dramatic
forbidden: neutral reporting verbs as the only verb
example: He storms across the yard, screaming, ready to burn the barn to the ground!
register_note: Brief 11, Task 3: ONE marker (extreme word or intensifier) plus the required punctuation is dramatic; the second marker group is style advice, not an admission criterion.

label: Business
example: Q3 target achieved: 47 metres to the barn, zero delays, full alignment.
register_note: Brief 9, Task 6: exactly ONE marker from each group — more markers do not make it more Business, they make it a parody of a memo. The sentence stays a real, dry update about this scene.

label: Gossip
forbidden: gossip about a real named person
example: Bestie, you won't believe it - she told me he walked into that barn like he owns it.
register_note: Brief 9, Task 6: exactly ONE hook and ONE attribution, and the listener and event are REAL — a friend is being told something that happened, never markers pasted in front of a description.

label: Nerd
example: The male, having secured the yard, advances toward the barn, where the flock is kept.

label: Flirt
forbidden: any reference to a body or body part
any line addressed to or about a minor
example: Okay but the way he walks into that barn? Kind of impressive, not gonna lie.
register_note: Brief 9, Task 7: the second-person requirement LEADS the style block — the sentence is spoken TO the person in the scene, never about them; a draft with no you/your is not Flirt.
safety_note: Youngest user is 13. Compliment actions, skills, style, taste, energy, confidence only.

label: Low IQ
forbidden: a claim nobody could believe (hair is made of clock, barns are made of chicken) — word salad, not comedy
countability errors: a/an on an uncountable noun, made of + a bare singular countable noun
mocking a person, nationality or job
example: A ponytail is hair. The hair is on her head, so that is where the ponytail is.
register_note: Brief 9, Task 2: vacuously obvious, not surreal. Exactly one of two moves: (1) a vacuously obvious statement — completely true, says nothing, usually circular ('The chair is for sitting. That is why she sits on it.'); (2) a believable mistake — a wrong idea a real person could hold, usually from confusing two similar things ('A ponytail is a small horse.'). The test: could a real person say this and mean it? If no, it is nonsense, not Low IQ. Because vacuous sentences are true, the register cannot teach the learner anything false.
